**Group:** Artifacts  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A non-biological imaging artifact: a frame that is out of focus or motion-blurred so that no sharp edges or cellular detail are resolvable — the subject, if any, is smeared or hazy. Use for images too blurred to classify. Exclude from analysis. Key features: overall softness/smearing, no crisp outlines or internal structure.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **dense** | The Dense detritus class is a solid, sharply-bounded opaque particle; a Blur artifact is soft and smeared throughout with no crisp edge. |
| **aggregate** | An aggregate still has resolvable particles and edges even when fluffy; a Blur artifact has no resolvable structure at all. |
